title: Chapter 86
content:
Stepping across the threshold of the main estate, the hostility in the air was palpable.

Seated in the grand salon, Kim Sun-young pinned Il-hyun beneath a cold, razor-sharp glare.

"Enjoying good health, Mother?"

"Arriving unannounced without a single word?" she countered, her voice ice.

Surrounded by unmasked contempt, Il-hyun merely offered an easy, polished smile. "I came to pay Father a visit. He's upstairs in the study, I assume?"

"He is occupied with business. Come back another time."

Ignoring her completely, Il-hyun turned and ascended the sweeping staircase. Sun-young’s jaw tightened in displeasure, but she lacked the authority to physically bar his way.

Reaching the upper landing, he strode to Chairman Kang’s private study, knocked twice, and turned the heavy brass handle without waiting for permission.

Engaged in a hushed consultation with Chief Secretary Kim, Chairman Kang snapped his gaze toward the door. A flash of raw, bitter distaste broke across the old man's face before vanishing behind his stoic mask.

Il-hyun unbuttoned his tailored suit jacket, sinking into the leather armchair opposite the desk with fluid grace.

"Dropping in without an appointment. What brings you here?"

"Mother greeted me with those exact words," Il-hyun mused smoothly. "Does a son require formal justification to visit his own father?"

"I am in no mood for your insolence today. Get out."

Il-hyun offered no verbal reply, resting his chin on his fingers as he held the Chairman’s stare. The tension stretched like a wire on the verge of snapping.

Unable to stomach the defiance, Chairman Kang gave Secretary Kim a subtle tilt of his chin.

The secretary bowed, stepping toward the armchair. "President Kang. It would be best if you took your leave for the day."

When Il-hyun remained motionless, Secretary Kim reached out, grasping his forearm. "President Kang—"

In a blinding flash of motion, Il-hyun withdrew the matte-black automatic from his breast pocket, leveling the barrel squarely at the secretary's foot.

BANG!

A concussive, ear-splitting report ruptured the quiet study.

The heavy slug punched clean through Secretary Kim’s dress shoe, shattering bone. A strangled shriek tore from the man's throat as he collapsed onto the Persian rug, clutching his mangled foot.

Chairman Kang surged to his feet in shock.

Within seconds, the heavy double doors were kicked wide as three burly private security enforcers spilled into the study, sidearms drawn.

Il-hyun tossed the smoking pistol carelessly onto the low table. With slow, deliberate flicks of his fingers, he brushed off the sleeve Secretary Kim had dared to touch.

One guard rushed to haul the bleeding secretary down the hall, while the remaining two posted themselves behind Il-hyun's chair, eyes locked on the Chairman, awaiting the order to execute.

Il-hyun draped an arm along the sofa back, offering a lazy, tranquil grin.

"Don't touch me. Lay a single finger on my skin, and I'll butcher everyone in this room into neat little steaks."

Though delivered to the guards, his dark, reptilian gaze was locked dead onto Chairman Kang.

Trembling with rage, the patriarch snatched the discarded pistol from the mahogany table, racking the slide and aiming the muzzle straight between Il-hyun’s eyes.

Il-hyun didn't even blink. His smile only widened.

"Pull it."

The muscle beneath the Chairman's left eye twitched violently.

"You... you unhinged, psychopathic bastard!"

"Are you afraid of me, Father?"

Caught off balance by the blunt truth, the old man’s jaw clamped into rigid stone, his gray irises burning with lethal, desperate malice.

Il-hyun repeated the question, his voice a smooth, mocking purr:

"Tell me. Does your own flesh and blood terrify you? Do I look like a monster in your eyes?"

Chairman Kang’s index finger tightened against the trigger guard, trembling with tension.

Il-hyun chuckled softly, rising to his full height.

"I gave you your chance."

Tugging his lapels straight, Il-hyun adjusted his cuffs and turned, sauntering toward the exit with effortless swagger.

The moment his fingers brushed the brass latch, a sharp metallic noise echoed from behind:

Click.

Il-hyun stopped, slowly looking back over his shoulder.

Chairman Kang stood frozen with the gun leveled, looking utterly stunned—having just pulled the trigger.

The old man's cheek twitched with shock, prompting a dry, condescending laugh to slip past Il-hyun’s lips.

"Seems your instincts have grown dreadfully dull in your old age, Father."

The weapon had been loaded with a single round—the very bullet currently lodged in Secretary Kim’s metatarsals.

Humiliated, the Chairman pulled the trigger repeatedly in a frantic frenzy: Click, click, click. The empty firing pin dropped against the hollow chamber.

Realizing he had been thoroughly toyed with, Chairman Kang’s face flushed a violent, apoplectic purple. With a guttural roar, he hurled the heavy steel frame across the room.

The pistol struck the heavy door frame with a loud thud, clattering to the parquet floor.

Il-hyun stared down at the weapon, his expression draining into a cold, clinical void.

"Family members must never inflict physical harm upon one another," Il-hyun recited, quoting the syndicate's founding code with the detached cadence of a magistrate reading a death sentence.

"..."

"However... should one strike first, they must be prepared to endure the exact same retribution."

A chilling, demonic smirk carved across Il-hyun’s face.

"Since you took a shot at me today, Father... next time, the turn is mine."

Chairman Kang snatched a heavy crystal ashtray, hurling it with all his might. Il-hyun ducked the projectile effortlessly, offered a crisp, mocking nod of his head, and slipped out into the hallway.

Behind the heavy oak doors, deafening roars of fury and the sound of shattered luxury decor shook the upper floor.

Walking down the long corridor, the polished smile faded entirely from Il-hyun’s features, leaving behind a dark, tempestuous storm of pure hatred.
Perched on the sill of his bedroom window, Jakyeong chain-smoked in brooding silence, staring into the dark courtyard.

Wang Ryun remained completely oblivious to his lover's betrayal. Jakyeong had reached out to every underground contact in his ledger, but the response was unanimous: Yoon Mi-ra had vanished off the face of the earth.

To spend years whispering sweet nothings, only to trade a man's life for a duffel bag of cash...

Since returning to the estate, he and Wang Han had racked their brains for a solution, ultimately settling the dilemma with a grim game of rock-paper-scissors to decide who would deliver the devastating news. Thankfully, Han had lost.

Snubbing out the filter, Jakyeong opened the casement to flush the haze, then collapsed across the king-sized mattress. Having pulled an involuntary all-nighter under gunfire, exhaustion claimed him the moment his head hit the pillow.

Yet sleep brought no peace. The phantom of the previous night played on a loop behind his eyelids: the young, terrified face beneath the balaclava morphing into his own reflection, coughing up mouthfuls of crimson before plunging into the dark.

A soft click of the latch and approaching footsteps dragged him from the nightmare.

Blinking through the heavy grogginess, he pushed himself up to find Kang Il-hyun pulling an armchair up to the bedside.

The man’s sharp, handsome features looked thoroughly worn down—shadowed by a deep, hollow fatigue.

"The staff mentioned you skipped dinner to sleep, so I came up to check on you."

Jakyeong glanced at the bedside clock: past eight in the evening. He rubbed his face to clear the fog, wincing as a sharp pang pulled at his wounded forearm.

Il-hyun caught the wrist immediately, turning the limb over to inspect the clean line of surgical sutures across the muscle.

"Did you have trouble washing up?" Il-hyun asked, his baritone softening.

"Han-ge helped me rinse off."

The moment the words cleared his lips, Il-hyun’s dark brow arched into a sharp, displeased peak.

Jakyeong reached for a clean t-shirt on the nightstand, only for Il-hyun’s hand to clamp down onto his shoulder, pinning him in place. The ominous, sour glint returning to those dark irises signaled that another petty offense had been registered.

"Is it standard practice for brothers to wash each other's bodies?"

"When someone's wounded, obviously. Besides, Han-ge practically raised me. He gave me baths all the time when I was ten."

Scowling, Il-hyun rose, marched over to the writing desk, and returned with a notepad and a fountain pen.

Jakyeong watched in utter confusion as Il-hyun thrust the stationary into his lap.

"Rank them," Il-hyun demanded flatly.

"Excuse me?"

"Wang Han, Wang Ryun, and me. Rank us in order of personal importance."

Jakyeong’s face contorted in disbelief. Waking up to find a lunatic demanding a popularity hierarchy felt entirely surreal.

When Jakyeong hesitated, Il-hyun leaned in with a heavy, suffocating glare, practically forcing the pen between his fingers.

God, here we go again.

Deciding to end the nonsense quickly, Jakyeong scribbled Wang Han at the very top, jotted Wang Ryunbeneath it, and scrawled Kang Il-hyun at the bottom of the page.

He thrust the pad forward.

Il-hyun stared at the ranking, his jaw grinding with an audible crunch.

Snatching the pen, Il-hyun drew two thick, violent slashes straight through Wang Han and Wang Ryun’s names, then looked up with a radiant, cheerful smile.

"If I slaughter both of them, I take first place by default. Right?"

Jakyeong snatched the pad back, crumpling the sheet into a ball.

And here I thought he was acting like a sane, civilized gentleman this morning...

A total waste of sympathy. The psychopath is back in full force.

Refusing to engage further, Jakyeong pulled the duvet over his head, curling away.

"Get out. I'm going back to sleep."

"Tell me what you need, darling."

A large hand began worming its way beneath the blanket, brushing against his waist.

"Money? Hmm? You love cash, don't you?"

"..."

"I have more wealth than you could spend in ten lifetimes."

"..."

"If I liquidate everything and hand it over to you... will you put me first?"

Losing his temper, Jakyeong kicked the duvet aside, shoved Il-hyun back by the shoulders, and slid off the mattress.

He opened the concealed floor safe beneath the wardrobe, pulled out three thick, banded bricks of US hundred-dollar bills, and strode back to the bed.

Seizing Il-hyun by the collar, the tailored silk buttons popped, tearing the fabric open. Jakyeong shoved the stacks of cash straight down the front of Il-hyun's shirt.

"I'll give you the damn money," Jakyeong hissed. "Just get the fuck out of my room."

Pulling the bricks from his chest, Il-hyun’s eyes narrowed into sharp, dangerous slits.

"Quite the practiced technique, darling. You seem remarkably comfortable stuffing cash down another man's shirt."

Tossing the money to the floor, Il-hyun lunged, straddling Jakyeong’s hips on the mattress.

In the scuffle, he gripped Jakyeong's injured forearm too tightly, drawing a sharp, pained hiss from the boy's throat.

Il-hyun let go instantly, murmuring a soft, genuinely apologetic, "Sorry..." before melting forward, burying his face into Jakyeong’s chest like a needy, spoiled child.

Jakyeong debated pulling a fistful of dark hair to shove him off, but seeing the exhaustion in the man's posture, his fingers relaxed.

"Stop pushing me away... Just hold me," Il-hyun mumbled into the cotton of his shirt. "I had a dreadful, exhausting day today."

Watching a towering, broad-shouldered monolith clinging to him like a lost stray was thoroughly absurd. Jakyeong expected him to pull away after a few seconds, but the man remained completely motionless.

When Jakyeong quietly asked what had happened, Il-hyun gave no reply.

Sighing, Jakyeong carefully draped his uninjured arm over the broad back, letting his hand rest against the tailored shoulder.

Ten minutes passed in absolute stillness. Then twenty.

"Lee Ja-kyeong."

The low baritone broke the quiet room.

"Speak. I'm listening."

If he starts bragging about his net worth again, I'm throwing a punch.

"I own a private estate in Hawaii."

From cash flexes to real estate flexes.

"Would you like to stay there for a while?"

The unexpected proposition made Jakyeong’s eyes widen. Is he suggesting a vacation?

Looking down, Il-hyun lifted his head. His handsome lips carried a faint smile, but beneath the surface, his dark pupils were as calm, heavy, and pitch-black as the sky before a catastrophic typhoon.

"A month should suffice. Consider it an extended holiday."
